transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-19
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Rafael Ortiz (Redwood SE); Jordan Park (Redwood SE); Anika Rao (Evobridge CTO); Marcus Bell (Evobridge Sr Eng); Li Wei (Head of Platform); Sophie Duarte (SecOps)

Auto-summary: Evobridge is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted + dedicated capacity. Primary concerns: integration with their gateway/proxy pattern, SDK compatibility (LangChain / LlamaIndex), rate limit/quotas model, and observability hooks (trace/span correlation, token-level cost). They want to understand tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC) for latency vs cost and compliance.

Topics: SDKs and connectors; gateway/proxy design; rate limiting and quotas; telemetry/observability hooks; security (KMS, SSO/SAML, SOC2); pilot scope and benchmarks.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick rollcall, I'm Maya Chen, AE at Redwood. Rafael and Jordan are with me from our infra team.
[00:10] Anika: Hi Maya, thanks. Anika here, CTO at Evobridge. Marcus and Li on from our side, and Sophie joined for security questions.
[00:20] Rafael: Nice to meet you all. High level today we want to understand your existing gateway and how you'd integrate our SDKs or proxy patterns, and then line up a pilot.
[00:30] Li: Sure. Quick context — we run a microservices mesh on EKS, with an API gateway in front of it. We already have a proxy that normalizes requests for downstream ML services. The ask is: can Redwood plug seamlessly as an upstream model service, what SDKs are required, and how do we manage quotas per tenant?
[00:45] Marcus: Also, we have a hard 100ms p50 SLO for conversational features; many queries are short but there are long context ones too. We care about KV cache TTLs because some conversations reuse tokens heavily.
[00:58] Jordan: Got it. For latency needs you might look at Dedicated or Private. Hosted can be fast but with variable tail latencies depending on multi-tenancy; Dedicated gives you reserved pools and more predictable p95s.
[01:15] Anika: We expected that. Can you explain the integration patterns? We currently use LangChain and are experimenting with LlamaIndex for retrieval.
[01:27] Rafael: Sure — there are two main patterns we see. 1) Direct SDK calls from your app to Redwood hosted endpoints using our SDKs (python/js), which LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters can talk to via our connectors. 2) Proxy/gateway approach: your gateway forwards requests to a sidecar or service that handles batching, caching, and routing to Redwood; this is useful when you need per-tenant quotas or local pre-/post-processing.
[01:50] Marcus: If we go proxy, can we still use LangChain primitives or will we need to change the call shapes?
[01:58] Rafael: You can keep LangChain on the client side; the proxy just acts as a shim. Example: LangChain calls your local adapter that translates to whatever your proxy expects, proxy handles batching and sends a Redwood-compatible payload. We have sample adapters for LongChain — sorry, LangChain — and LlamaIndex plus an official proxy sample repo.
[02:20] Li: What's the recommended way to do per-tenant rate limits? We need quotas enforced in the gateway and also accurate cost attribution.
[02:28] Jordan: Two layers — token-level quotas enforced by Redwood at the billing layer, and gateway rate-limits for throttling. We expose headers with token counts and model variant IDs so your gateway can make decisions. Also our SDK emits usage metrics to your observability sink if you integrate the hooks.
[02:45] Sophie: On compliance, we require SAML SSO, audit logs, KMS integration for key wrapping, and SOC2. Are these supported in Hosted?
[02:56] Maya: Hosted supports SSO/SAML and we provide audit logs and an option to integrate with external KMS for Private and Dedicated; hosted can do KMS via managed keys but for certain compliance customers we recommend Dedicated or Private for customer-controlled keys. We can share SOC2 and ISO artifacts — Rafael, will you drop the security pack link?
[03:14] Rafael: Yes, I'll attach the docs. Also note for Private (VPC) deployments we can do customer-managed KMS/HSM and tighter network controls.
[03:25] Marcus: Another question: we run embeddings for vector search; we want to pipeline embeddings through LlamaIndex. Can Redwood provide batched embed endpoints with lower cost per unit?
[03:36] Rafael: Embedding endpoints support batching and can be routed to quantized model variants which reduce cost. For heavy embedding pipelines we often suggest Dedicated pools with autoscaling for throughput predictability.
[03:48] Anika: For a pilot, can you run on our representative dataset and give latency/cost numbers?
[03:54] Maya: Absolutely. Typical pilot flow: you provide traces + sample payloads, we run a benchmark on Hosted and on a Dedicated config, return p50/p95 and token cost estimates, then we iterate. Rafael will own the bench.
[04:08] Marcus: About observability — we use Datadog and Honeycomb. We need span correlation between our requests and Redwood tokens so we can attribute costs in traces.
[04:18] Jordan: We support standard OpenTelemetry headers, and we can emit token-level metrics to your metrics backplane. There's a small SDK hook that annotates traces with model, variant, token_count, and request_id. That should let Honeycomb correlate traces.
[04:33] Sophie: Are audit logs exportable to our SIEM?
[04:36] Maya: Yes, we can stream audit events to your S3 or ingest them into SIEM via a connector. For Dedicated/Private you get retention and direct ingestion; hosted has configurable retention windows.
[04:47] Anika: Can you summarize the tradeoffs between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for our use?
[04:52] Rafael: Hosted: fastest to try, simpler SDK integration, good for prototyping but variable tail latency and shared KMS. Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, predictable latency and throughput, better cost-per-token at scale, supports customer KMS integration and stronger isolation. Private (VPC/on-prem): full network isolation, customer-managed keys and air-gapped deployments — higher setup time and ops cost but required for regulated data.
[05:15] Li: What about fallbacks? If Dedicated pool is saturated during traffic spikes, do you have automatic fallback?
[05:21] Jordan: Yes, we support routing policies with automatic fallback to compatible model variants or to Hosted. You can set cost vs latency policies per route.
[05:30] Marcus: On model variants — do you do quantized variants automatically? We have throughput spikes; quantization might affect quality.
[05:38] Rafael: We provide recommended quantization profiles per model and workload. For retrieval-augmented tasks we usually keep higher-precision models for final responses but use quantized variants for heavy embedding or low-cost pipelines. We also support A/B rollouts to monitor quality regressions.
[05:55] Anika: Let's talk connectors — do you have first-class LangChain and LlamaIndex integrations or are they community adapters?
[06:02] Rafael: We maintain official connectors for LangChain (open-source) and an official LlamaIndex adapter. They live in our SDK repo; Jordan can drop links. The adapters handle caching, retry policies, and token accounting so you don't have to re-implement.
[06:20] Jordan: Link: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-adapters (will share after). Also sample proxy repo: github.com/redwood-inference/proxy-sample.
[06:30] Sophie: For tenant isolation, is data ever persisted on Redwood-managed storage? We need clear data residency and deletion controls.
[06:38] Maya: By default, we retain request metadata for billing and diagnostics for a configurable retention. For Private and Dedicated you can opt into no-persistence or customer-managed storage, and we support data deletion APIs and retention policies.
[06:55] Marcus: About quotas — can we set per-API-key or per-tenant daily token quotas and have the gateway preempt calls?
[07:03] Jordan: Yes. You can enforce soft and hard quotas. Soft quota returns warn headers and can trigger throttling in your gateway; hard quota returns 429. We also surface quota consumption metrics in the console and via webhooks.
[07:16] Anika: Latency numbers — what p95 should we expect for Dedicated vs Hosted for short convo queries?
[07:22] Rafael: For short queries with warm KV cache, Dedicated p50 ~ 30-40ms for optimized models on A100/80GB equiv with continuous batching disabled; p95 depends on sequence length but typically under 120ms. Hosted p95 will be higher and less predictable due to multi-tenant interference — maybe 150-300ms depending on region and load. We'll confirm with a benchmark.
[07:48] Sophie: On encryption: do you support customer-managed keys in Hosted?
[07:52] Maya: Hosted supports managed keys; for truly customer-controlled KMS you should look at Dedicated or Private. We can do envelope encryption and key wrapping with external KMS for Private.
[08:05] Marcus: Integration detail: does the SDK expose incremental streaming and function/tool calling hooks? We rely on streaming to reduce TTF.
[08:13] Rafael: Yes, SDK supports streaming responses and function call structured output. We also provide examples for building streaming adapters into LangChain chains.
[08:26] Anika: Anything special about rate limit headers or the exact header names so our gateway can parse them?
[08:32] Jordan: We'll provide a header spec, but typical headers: x-rw-usage-tokens, x-rw-model-variant, x-rw-req-id, x-rw-quota-left. They are consistent across SDKs.
[08:45] Li: We also want per-route observability — model-level cost and latency breakdowns per tenant visible in our dashboard. Can Redwood forward per-route metrics?
[08:54] Rafael: Yes, we can stream per-route telemetry. For Dedicated you can get token-level breakdowns and route mapping exported to your metrics backend. There's also an ingestion feature to push metrics to Datadog/Grafana.
[09:08] Marcus: For the pilot, we need to test a real mix of short intent queries and long context generations with retrieval. Will Redwood's caching honor prefix caching for multi-turn convos so token counts reduce over time?
[09:22] Jordan: We support prefix/KV caching that persists KV cache for a session; you'll see fewer compute tokens for repeated prefixes. We'll need to align TTLs and session keys with your proxy.
[09:35] Anika: On cost — can you give a rough per-1M-token cost delta hosted vs dedicated?
[09:42] Maya: It's workload dependent but ballpark Dedicated can be 20-40% cheaper per-token at scale due to reserved capacity and optimized kernels. We'll run your traces to give a specific delta.
[09:55] Sophie: Security review — can you describe the audit trail fields for each request? We need user_id, request_id, model_variant, token_count, and timestamp at minimum.
[10:05] Rafael: Yes, those are part of the audit schema. We'll share the schema in the security pack.
[10:12] Anika: About rollout strategy — we want canary then gradual ramp if quality holds. Do you support canary routing by percentage in the console?
[10:20] Jordan: Yes, rollouts allow canary percentages, automatic rollback on regression signals, and route-level weights.
[10:28] Marcus: What about telemetry retention? We need 90 days of detailed metrics for auditing.
[10:34] Maya: Dedicated offers configurable retention; hosted defaults to 30 days. We can add an add-on for 90-day retention.
[10:43] Li: Are there any SDK limitations for our node-based gateway? We prefer a lightweight adapter in Go/Node.
[10:50] Rafael: We have official node and python SDKs; community-contributed Go adapters exist. For the gateway you can use our HTTP interface directly or use the Node SDK; for Go we can share a sample shim.
[11:02] Anika: Ok let's align on the pilot scope and timeline. We'd like a 2-week pilot, run both Hosted and Dedicated bench runs, and then decide.
[11:12] Maya: Sounds good. Proposed next steps: Evobridge shares traces + a sample dataset; Redwood runs Hosted benchmark and a Dedicated sizing bench; we return results and a starter pricing estimate.
[11:22] Marcus: We'll anonymize traces and send by end of week.
[11:26] Sophie: I'll start the compliance questionnaire concurrently.
[11:28] Jordan: We'll also prepare a sample proxy repo tailored to your gateway patterns and include LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter examples.
[11:36] Anika: Great. Any outstanding blockers?
[11:40] Maya: None from our side. Rafael, anything for the bench we need?
[11:44] Rafael: Just the traces and token distribution, and indicate the model families you want tested. We'll default to 7B and 13B quantized and a higher-precision 33B for quality checks.
[11:55] Li: One more: can we schedule a deeper technical deep dive with our infra team next Tues?
[11:59] Maya: Yes, Rafael and Jordan can join. I'll propose times.
[12:03] Anika: Thanks all, good session.

Recap / Close:
- Evobridge to provide anonymized traces + SLOs (Marcus) by 2026-11-22.
- Maya to send pricing + Dedicated sizing worksheet by 2026-11-23.
- Rafael to schedule benchmark and provide run instructions (target completed by 2026-11-25).
- Sophie to circulate compliance questionnaire and request SOC2 docs (target 2026-11-24).
- Redwood to share SDK adapter links and proxy sample repo.

Shared artifacts referenced:
